title: Kohli's Twenty-Five-Ball Fifty Sealed It. RCB Have Won Back-to-Back IPL Titles.
excerpt: Royal Challengers Bengaluru chased down 156 with 14 balls to spare at the Narendra Modi Stadium, becoming only the third franchise to successfully defend the IPL crown.
body:
Royal Challengers Bengaluru have won the IPL 2026 final. They beat Gujarat Titans by five wickets at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad on Sunday night, chasing down 156 in 17.6 overs to become only the third franchise in IPL history to successfully defend the title.

Virat Kohli scored the fastest fifty of his IPL career — off just 25 balls — to anchor the chase after wickets fell in clusters around him. His half-century in the 12th over, brought up with a pull shot off Arshad Khan, ended a ten-year wait for a fifty in an IPL playoff match. His last had come in the 2016 final against Sunrisers Hyderabad.

## RCB's Bowlers Set the Platform

Rajat Patidar, captaining his first IPL final, won the toss and chose to bowl. His bowlers rewarded the decision immediately. Josh Hazlewood removed Shubman Gill for 10 in the third over. Bhuvneshwar Kumar dismissed Sai Sudharsan for 12 in the very next over. Gujarat's much-vaunted top order was 27 for 2 in the powerplay, and the innings never recovered its footing.

Rasikh Salam Dar was the pick of the attack, claiming three wickets for 27 runs from his four overs. His pace and movement proved too much for Gujarat's middle order. Krunal Pandya outfoxed Jos Buttler in the 13th over, ending a scratchy innings of 19. Only Washington Sundar, who finished unbeaten on 50 off 37 balls, offered sustained resistance. His third half-century of the IPL 2026 season was a lone battle. Around him, Nishant Sindhu made 20 and no other Gujarat batter passed 15.

Gujarat Titans closed their innings at 155 for 8. At the same venue in the league stage, they had chased down 155 against RCB in 15.5 overs. This time, their bowlers needed to be near-perfect. They were not.

## The Fastest Start in IPL Final History

Kohli and Venkatesh Iyer opened the chase with startling intent. Kohli smashed 23 off his first eight deliveries. Iyer, matching him stroke for stroke, hit 26 off 13 balls. The pair reached the team fifty in just 3.3 overs — the fastest in any IPL final, breaking Chennai Super Kings' record of four overs at this same ground in 2023.

By the end of the fourth over, RCB were 55 without loss and the contest already felt decided.

Mohammed Siraj dismissed Iyer for 32 off 16, and Kagiso Rabada removed Devdutt Padikkal to give Gujarat a flicker of hope. But at 70 for 2 at the powerplay, RCB were firmly in control.

## Rashid Khan's Brief Fightback

Rashid Khan gave Gujarat one last surge, taking two wickets across consecutive overs to reduce RCB to 100 for 4 at the halfway mark. The Ahmedabad crowd, which had been relatively subdued through Gujarat's batting, found its voice.

It did not last. Kohli, who had batted through the chaos at the other end, was unmoved. Tim David joined him and immediately counterpunched, striking boundaries to keep the asking rate manageable. Arshad Khan eventually dismissed David for 24, but by then the damage was done. RCB needed just 24 off the final six overs.

Kohli finished the job without drama. RCB reached 161 for 5 with 14 balls remaining.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the millions of Indian cricket fans watching from living rooms in New Jersey, pubs in London, and late-night streams in Sydney, this final delivered a storyline the IPL rarely manages to write twice in a row. Kohli, 37, has now amassed more than 650 runs this season — a century and five fifties across 16 matches — and is on track for a record third Orange Cap.

RCB join Mumbai Indians (2019–2020) and Chennai Super Kings (2010–2011) as the only franchises to win consecutive IPL titles. For a club that went its first 16 seasons without a single trophy, two in a row is a shift in identity that no amount of "ee sala cup namde" memes could have predicted.

The IPL 2026 season began on March 28. It ended 65 days later with Kohli standing in the middle of the Narendra Modi Stadium, bat raised, a final that felt less like a contest and more like a coronation.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar finished the tournament as one of the most economical seamers in the competition. Hazlewood's bounce on the Ahmedabad surface proved unplayable in the powerplay. And Rasikh Salam Dar, the 22-year-old from Jammu and Kashmir who was playing his first IPL final, produced the spell that broke the game open.

The IPL now pauses. India's men next turn their attention to the Test and ODI series against Afghanistan. For RCB's diaspora faithful, the celebrations will last rather longer.
author: Diaspora Desk
